newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil SEC seeks return to inflation-adj results.
newsitem.headline: Brazil SEC seeks return to inflation-adj results.

text.p: Brazil's securities watchdog has proposed a return to the use of inflation-adjusted figures in company financial results, financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.

Gazeta said the change proposed in Brazil's Corporate Law was included in a bill prepared by a group of capital markets consultants under the direction of Brazil's Securities Commission, known by its Portuguese acronym, CVM.
The bill also would require privately held firms to publish their results.

Before the 1994 Real Plan was implemented, publicly traded firms were required to report inflation-adjusted results. The law was changed to the use of non-adjusted figures as the sharp drop in inflation under the plan seemed to make price adjustment unnecessary.
Moreover, private companies are not required by law to make their results public.
The newspaper said the CVM wanted a return to the use of inflation-adjustment to make Brazilian corporate results comparable to earnings worldwide.
